text:
Jordan: Kicking off a small canary in the 02:00-03:00 UTC window. Plan: API v5.1 (pin), runtime v2.3.0, console v1.8.0, router v3.2.0. Rollout staged: runtime -> console -> router, API pinned. Please ack any cross-service blockers and confirm rollback thresholds.

deploy-bot: /deploy canary runtime:v2.3.0 --stages=runtime,console,router --window=02:00-03:00UTC
Checklist: health-checks enabled, telemetry hooks set, canary=%5, auto-rollback=true. See runbook: https://internal.redwood/release/runbooks/canary-checklist

Maya: noted. runtime change includes kernel batch optimization + small kv-cache eviction tweak. Confirmed CPU mem footprint looks fine in perf runs. :white_check_mark:

Liam: router v3.2 has header-split flag change (X-RW-Route). We need a quick contract check: console must pass header handshake or fallback to legacy route. Sophie can you confirm console accepts new header?

Sophie: console accepts it behind a feature flag, not enabled in prod by default. I can flip on feature flag for canary scope if we want. Will add a canary-only flag to the rollout.

Jordan: Good — add console feature-flag for headers. That preserves safe handshake. Update release notes to call out header flag + how to revert.

Kai: Quick note on routing: if router sees unknown header, it currently falls back to route-v2. We should ensure fallback doesn't route to runtime v2.2.0 instances; set router pin mappings to prefer runtime v2.3.0 for canary traffic.

Liam: adding a temporary route-map: `router:set-map --canary runtime:v2.3.0 -> route-prefer` will be applied during canary window. I'll push the route-map and share diff.

Sophie: release notes draft: "Console: opt-in header-split (canary), how to toggle in UI and via API. Runtime: kernel batching opt-in on v2.3.0. Router: header-based preference mapping." Will post link in a minute.

Maya: rollback criteria proposal: abort and roll back if: 1) p50 inference latency increase > 25% over baseline for canary traffic for 10m, 2) 5xx rate > 1% absolute, 3) error budget burn > 30% in 15m. Any objections?

Jordan: Sounds reasonable. Add an additional safety: if cross-service tail latency (API->runtime->router) p99 increases > 40% over baseline for 5m, rollback immediate. Also, pin API to v5.1 during canary and do not rotate API versions until canary fully passes.

deploy-bot: Canary started: runtime:v2.3.0 -> console:v1.8.0 -> router:v3.2.0; api pinned at v5.1. Canary traffic = 5%. Health checks: ok. Telemetry: enabled. Will auto-rollback on thresholds.

Maya: Observability note: create a temporary dashboard tile showing cross-service trace latency (span:api->runtime->router) and canary label. I'll share once live.

Liam: route-map diff: https://internal.redwood/changes/4721 (applied). Router metrics look normal so far.

Sophie: release-notes link: https://internal.redwood/notes/2134 (draft posted). Includes revert steps and feature-flag toggle snippet.

Jordan: Thanks. Everyone please watch the dashboard for first 15 minutes. If no regressions, we'll promote canary to 25% then 100% per rollout plan. If you see issues drop a short message here with metric + time. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Canary progress: 5% -> 5% (15m). No auto-rollback triggers.

Kai: Confirmed fallback mapping prevents traffic to v2.2.0 during canary.

Jordan: Ack. Will wait for 15m stable signal then escalate to 25%. Stand by in thread.
